steps: Herbs and shrubs grow in the understory of forests, beneath the canopy of taller sun plants.
The canopy leaves absorb most of the red and blue light for photosynthesis.
The light that penetrates the canopy and reaches the forest floor is enriched in green wavelengths.
Green light is less efficiently absorbed by chlorophyll compared to red and blue light.
Therefore, the rate of photosynthesis in shade-dwelling herbs and shrubs is lower due to the quality of light received.
